title: Do pcell-mwall's intrinsic deaths still select heritable yield once remnant double counts are removed and the neutral-trait twin runs on three seeds?
summary: An independent audit (audit.md) found S, I, D and H emergent in pcell-mwall: no death or division rule exists, a neutral-trait twin (ytrait=2, seed 7) has no mature deaths and no yield rise, the rise is between cells, and daughters breed true (r 0.97-0.98). But the genealogy's MINP=20 death criterion records a shrinking cell as dead and its remnant as a new low-ranked cell that dies again, inflating death counts about 2x and producing the claim's 'low-born die more on 4/4 seeds' and 'already low at birth' (split-born cells only: pooled p=0.09; low yield is mostly acquired during life). About half the rise comes from faster growth of high-yield cells, not deaths. B, the M layer, is made by the cells' own catalysts and placed by an adsorption drift with no feedback; under RUBRIC L3's quasi-equilibrium clause it counts, but it does no work, and the claim's B control (bm=0) is not matched (chim=0 is).
experiment: On fresh seeds 21, 22 and 23, run the claim's world.py unchanged (ytrait=1) and its neutral-trait twin (ytrait=2: y inherited and mutated but every particle acts with y0), 100000 steps each, through the claim's genealogy.py. Replace genealogy deaths with a remnant-aware physical criterion: an 'appear' cell holding 3 or more uids of a cell recorded dead in the previous 2000 steps continues that lineage, and a lineage dies only when its uids form no phi>0.5 component with at least 5 particles for 2000 steps (files/physdeath.py, files/remnant.py). Count mature cells only (lived >= 10000 steps). Report per arm: physical mature deaths, their yield percentile at death and 2000 steps earlier against the marker z, split-born birth-rank fate, the Price death and growth terms, and particle-weighted mean y against z. Pass: on 3/3 seeds the claim arm has >= 6 physical mature deaths at mean yield percentile <= 0.15 (z 0.35-0.65) and mean y exceeds z by >= 0.10, while the twin has at most a third of the deaths and mean y within 0.05 of z. Fail: fewer than 3 physical mature deaths or percentile > 0.3 on 2+ seeds, or the twin dies as often. Publish the result as a review of 20261025T1345-c14-pcell-mwall-claim (cid c1) with per-capability verdicts.
